Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 91, verses 9–12:

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[9–12] ﴿He has certainly succeeded who purifies it, And he has certainly failed who instills it [with corruption]. Thamud denied [their prophet] in their transgression, when the most wretched of them broke forth.﴾

﴿He has certainly succeeded who purifies it﴾: that is, he purified his soul and cleansed it from the filth of deficiencies and sins; or he developed it through knowledge and action and its reaching perfection and attaining its original nature (al-fitrah al-ula). ﴿And he has certainly failed who instills it﴾: that is, he buried it and lowered it, by abandoning it from guidance until he committed sins and left the obedience of God, exalted is He. This is what Ibn Jarir said. Others said: that is, he diminished its purification and concealed its readiness and its natural disposition in which it was created, through ignorance and wickedness. It is derived from (dassa al-shay' fi al-turab), meaning he inserted it into the dust and concealed it. The original of (dassa) is (dassas), like (taqadda al-bazi). The clause "He has certainly succeeded" etc. is the answer to the oath, and the lam has been omitted due to the length [of the clause].

The judge (al-Qadi) said: It seems that when He intended by it to urge the perfecting of the soul and to emphasize it, He swore by that which points them to knowledge of the existence of the Creator, the necessity of His being, and the perfection of His attributes, which is the highest degree of the theoretical faculty, and reminds them of the greatness of God so as to move them to be absorbed in thanking His blessings, which is the ultimate perfection of the practical faculty.

Al-Zamakhshari held that this clause is a statement that follows His saying: ﴿And inspired it with its wickedness and its righteousness﴾ [91:8], by way of digression. The answer to the oath is omitted, its estimated sense being: "God will surely destroy them," that is, the people of Makkah, for their denial of the Messenger of God ﷺ, just as He destroyed Thamud, because they denied Salih (peace be upon him).

This is indicated by His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Thamud denied [their prophet] in their transgression﴾ [91:11], that is, because of their transgression and their exceeding the limit in wickedness. So al-taghwa is a verbal noun. It is permissible that it means the punishment itself, either with an omitted modifier or without it, as an intensification, just as other verbal nouns are used as descriptions; that is, they denied the punishment with which they were threatened, which is characterized by transgression, as in His saying: ﴿So they were destroyed by the overwhelming [blast]﴾ [69:5]. Thus al-taghwa in this sense means exceeding the limit and increase in punishment. The preposition (bi) is connected to "denied." His saying, exalted is He: ﴿when the most wretched of them broke forth﴾ [91:12] is a temporal clause modifying "denied" or "transgression," that is, when the most wretched of Thamud rose to hamstring the she-camel of Salih (peace be upon him). They had been forbidden to touch her with harm, and had been warned of the consequence of disobedience, as He, exalted is He, said:

The judge (al-Qadi) said: It seems that when He intended by it to urge the perfecting of the soul and to emphasize it, He swore by that which points them to knowledge of the existence of the Creator, the necessity of His being, and the perfection of His attributes, which is the highest degree of the theoretical faculty, and reminds them of the greatness of God so as to move them to be absorbed in thanking His blessings, which is the ultimate perfection of the practical faculty.

Al-Zamakhshari held that this clause is a statement that follows His saying: ﴿And inspired it with its wickedness and its righteousness﴾ [91:8], by way of digression. The answer to the oath is omitted, its estimated sense being: "God will surely destroy them," that is, the people of Makkah, for their denial of the Messenger of God ﷺ, just as He destroyed Thamud, because they denied Salih (peace be upon him).

This is indicated by His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Thamud denied [their prophet] in their transgression﴾ [91:11], that is, because of their transgression and their exceeding the limit in wickedness. So al-taghwa is a verbal noun. It is permissible that it means the punishment itself, either with an omitted modifier or without it, as an intensification, just as other verbal nouns are used as descriptions; that is, they denied the punishment with which they were threatened, which is characterized by transgression, as in His saying: ﴿So they were destroyed by the overwhelming [blast]﴾ [69:5]. Thus al-taghwa in this sense means exceeding the limit and increase in punishment. The preposition (bi) is connected to "denied." His saying, exalted is He: ﴿when the most wretched of them broke forth﴾ [91:12] is a temporal clause modifying "denied" or "transgression," that is, when the most wretched of Thamud rose to hamstring the she-camel of Salih (peace be upon him). They had been forbidden to touch her with harm, and had been warned of the consequence of disobedience, as He, exalted is He, said:

Commentary on the interpretation of His saying, Exalted is He:

[13–15] ﴿So the Messenger of Allah said to them: "The she-camel of Allah, and her drinking [day]."﴾ ﴿But they denied him and hamstrung her, so their Lord crushed them over their sin and leveled them [all].﴾ [Ash-Shams: 14] ﴿And He does not fear its consequence.﴾ [Ash-Shams: 15]

﴿So the Messenger of Allah said to them﴾ means Salih, peace be upon him, to his people. ﴿The she-camel of Allah, and her drinking [day]﴾ means: beware of and guard against the she-camel of Allah, which He made a clear sign, and her drinking, which Allah singled out for her on her day. The Prophet, peace be upon him, had informed them, on the command of Allah, that the she-camel was to have a day of drinking and they were to have another day of drinking, apart from the day of the she-camel, as the verse of ash-Shu'ara' explains, where He says: ﴿This is a she-camel; she has a drinking [day], and you have a drinking day of a known time.﴾ [Ash-Shu'ara': 155] ﴿And do not touch her with harm, lest there seize you the punishment of a tremendous day.﴾ [Ash-Shu'ara': 156] That is: do not harm the she-camel, and do not transgress against her in her drinking or on her day of drinking. ﴿But they denied him﴾ [Ash-Shams: 14], that is, in what he warned them of regarding the descent of punishment if they did it. ﴿And hamstrung her﴾ [Ash-Shams: 14], that is, they killed her.

Al-Nihayah (the "End" – a dictionary of hadith terms by Ibn al-Athir) says: The original sense of 'aqr (hamstringing) is striking the legs of a camel or sheep with a sword while it stands. Then it broadened until it was used for killing and destruction. That is because they all agreed to prevent her from drinking and were content with her being killed. Whoever killed her or hamstrung her did so with the consent of all of them; therefore denial and hamstringing are attributed to all of them.

It was also said: "damdama" means the punishment enveloped them. It was also said: "al-damdamah" is an imitation of the sound of a crash. ﴿And leveled them﴾ [Ash-Shams: 14], that is, He leveled the destruction upon them all, so that not one of them escaped.

It means He made it equal among them; or the pronoun refers back to Thamud, meaning He made it equal upon them.

﴿And He does not fear its consequence﴾ [Ash-Shams: 15], that is, He does not fear the repercussion of their destruction, for He is the Mighty who cannot be overcome.

Al-Shihab (al-Khafaji) said: That is, He does not fear its outcome, as kings fear the outcome of what they do. It is permissible for it to refer back to the Messenger, peace be upon him, meaning that he does not fear the consequence of his warning to them, and this is literal. Likewise if it is said that the pronoun refers to the most wretched (al-ashqa), meaning he does not fear the consequence of his heinous deed.
